subject: dsa
title: Hand of Straights
summary: Sort the cards, then greedily build a run starting from the smallest card left. The smallest card must anchor some group, so its run is forced; if a needed card is missing, the split is impossible.
problem: Given a hand of cards and a groupSize, decide if the cards can be split into groups of that many consecutive numbers.

steps.caption: Can these cards split into groups of 3 consecutive numbers? Sort first, then greedily build a run starting from the smallest card left.
The smallest card is 1. To use it we need 1, 2, 3 for a run of three.
Found a 2 and a 3, so the first group {1, 2, 3} is complete.
The smallest card left is the other 2. Build a run 2, 3, 4 starting from it.
Found a 3 and a 4, so the second group {2, 3, 4} is complete.
Every card landed in a run of 3 consecutive numbers, so the split works. Answer: true.
